market_context: United States/general English; cooking frozen raw chicken without thawing
title: Can you cook chicken directly from frozen?

seo.title: Can you cook chicken directly from frozen?
seo.meta_description: Yes. Chicken can be cooked from frozen in the oven or on the stove, but it may take about 50% longer and must reach 165 °F internally.
seo.search_intent: Learn when cooking frozen chicken without thawing is safe and which methods should be avoided.

excerpt: USDA says chicken can be cooked from frozen in the oven or on the stove. Cooking may take about 50% longer, and the thickest part must reach at least 165 °F. USDA does not recommend starting raw frozen chicken in a slow cooker.
content_html:
You do not always have to thaw chicken before cooking. USDA says frozen chicken can be cooked safely in the oven or on the stove when it reaches 165 °F internally.

Plan on about 50% more time

Frozen chicken must first absorb enough heat to thaw internally before it can finish cooking. USDA estimates roughly one-and-a-half times the cooking time of thawed chicken.

A recipe that takes 30 minutes with thawed chicken might therefore take around 45 minutes from frozen, although thickness and method can move that number substantially.

Use a thermometer, not the clock

The thickest part must reach 165 °F (73.9 °C). Frozen pieces can brown outside while the center is still cold, making a thermometer especially important.

Oven and stove are acceptable; slow cooker is not

USDA allows oven or stovetop cooking from frozen but advises against putting raw frozen chicken directly into a slow cooker because it can warm too slowly through the bacterial danger zone.

Separated pieces cook more evenly

Individually frozen breasts or thighs are easier to manage than a solid frozen block. If pieces are stuck together, separate them once the outside loosens enough to do so safely.

Safe does not mean every recipe works equally well

Being able to cook chicken from frozen does not mean every method gives the same result. With a thick breast, the outside can dry while the center finishes heating; smaller pieces or dishes with sauce are usually easier to manage.

If a recipe depends on fast browning, stuffing a piece or very even doneness, thawing first may still be better for quality and control. Cooking from frozen is a useful option, not a universal replacement for planned thawing.

Bottom line

Yes, chicken can go from freezer to oven or stovetop. Allow extra time and verify 165 °F in the center rather than relying on surface color.

faq.question: How much longer does frozen chicken take?
faq.answer: USDA estimates about 50% longer than thawed chicken, although actual time depends on thickness and method.

faq.question: Can frozen chicken go in a slow cooker?
faq.answer: USDA advises against starting raw frozen chicken in a slow cooker because it warms too slowly.

faq.question: What internal temperature is required?
faq.answer: At least 165 °F in the thickest part, measured with a food thermometer.
